newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk parliament fixes date for Erbakan challenge.
newsitem.headline: Turk parliament fixes date for Erbakan challenge.

text.p: Turkish members of parliament on Thursday said they would take up an opposition bid on October 16 to topple Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan for a controversial trip to Libya.

"A decision has been taken to hold the debate on Wednesday, October 16," left-wing MP Husamettin Ozkan told Reuters. He said three opposition censure motions had been merged into one that the assembly would begin to hear on Wednesday.
"The prime minister was involved in an insult and scandal unprecedented in the history of the Turkish Republic," the main opposition Motherland Party (ANAP) said in its motion.
Two left-wing parties also tabled motions to bring down Erbakan after a trip to Libya last weekend that left Turkey open to scathing attacks from both his hosts and Ankara's close ally Washington.
Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi severely criticised Erbakan for Turkey's treatment of its Kurds during a joint news conference in a Bedouin tent in the city of Sirte.
Turkey's ambassador to Libya, who had been recalled for consultations following the visit, reported to the foreign ministry in Ankara on Thursday, Anatolian news agency said.

The ministry said the ambassador had been summoned to Libya's foreign ministry before returning to Turkey, which had said that Gaddafi's comments had been misunderstood and that he condemned all forms of terrorism.
The United States rebuked Erbakan for supporting Libya against Western charges of backing terrorism.

Erbakan, who heads a coalition with Tansu Ciller's conservative True Path Party, would have to resign after little more than three months as modern Turkey's first Islamist leader if he lost a censure vote.
He has 281 MPs, five more than the number needed to guarantee victory in the vote.
He was to give a televised address on all national channels at 2100 (1800) GMT on Thursday about his visits to Libya, Egypt and Nigeria, the prime ministry said.
